 August gains were fueled by robotaxi momentum, including Nevada approval for up to 5,000 Robotaxis and plans to launch the Cybercab publicly in Austin. [...] ## Tesla (TSLA) Stock Price Performance: Last 30 Days vs. Quarter

Over the 30-day window through August 25, 2026, Tesla shares advanced approximately 12.6%, climbing from a closing price of $313.03 on July 24 to about $352.42. The gain reflects a notable recovery after the stock fell to an intraday low of $297.38 on July 29, its lowest level of the year. [...] margin excluding regulatory credits slipped to 16.3%. Free cash flow turned negative at -$1.09 billion as capital expenditures jumped 142% to $5.79 billion. The stock dropped roughly 13% in the following session.

articles.title: TSLA Stock Rises Overnight: Analyst Sees Rebound This Week After EV Delivery Surge, But Calls Stock ‘Fully-Priced’
articles.summary:
Morgan Stanley analyst Andrew Percoco said Tesla’s Q2 deliveries beat sell-side consensus by 18% and marked the company’s highest auto growth rate since the third quarter of 2023. The firm maintained an ‘Equal Weight’ rating and a $415 price target on Tesla, implying a 6% upside from the current levels. [...] Shares of Tesla, Inc. (TSLA) rose 1% overnight late Sunday as investors weighed a sharp second-quarter (Q2) delivery rebound against an analyst warning that the stock still looks “fully-priced.”

TSLA stock rose 4% last week, snapping a two-week losing streak despite a 7% drop on Thursday.

## Gary Black Sees TSLA Rebound [...] “I expect TSLA stock to rebound this week as the sell-side climbs over one another to increase 2Q and FY’26 earnings ests,” Black said, adding that higher estimates “could boost TSLA price targets.” Still, Black said that the stock trades at a 2026 price-to-earnings multiple of over 200x, compared with expected long-term earnings per share (EPS) growth of about 35% for 2027-2032, leaving it at a 6x PEG ratio. That, he said, “continues to suggest TSLA is fully priced.”

articles.title: Tesla (TSLA) Shares Fall 21% in 30 Days After Sharp Q2 Miss
articles.summary:
Investors were rattled by Tesla's spending trajectory. Capital expenditures more than doubled sequentially to $5.79 billion, pushing free cash flow to negative $1.09 billion — the first quarterly cash burn in over two years. CFO Vaibhav Taneja confirmed full-year capex guidance of more than $25 billion and signaled that spending would increase further in the second half and over the next two to three years. Tesla also disclosed it is arranging up to $30 billion in debt capacity to fund its AI, [...] Tesla shares dropped approximately 21% over the past 30 days, slumping from around $393 to near $313, driven primarily by a sharply disappointing Q2 2026 earnings report.
 The sell-off was triggered by a massive earnings miss — adjusted EPS of $0.33 versus analyst estimates of $0.51 — alongside negative free cash flow for the first time in two years. [...] Over the last 30 days, Tesla shares fell approximately 21%, from a closing price of $393.45 on July 2 to an intraday level near $312.76 as of early August. The decline was concentrated in a single catastrophic session on July 23, when the stock plunged 14.5% — its worst single-day drop since mid-2025 — wiping out more than $140 billion in market capitalization in one day. The stock briefly touched levels not seen since August 2025 before stabilizing above $300.
